name: CA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Huffman is a well-funded incumbent in a D+13 district with $1.16 million on hand
Challenger Robin Littau shows no reported fundraising or visible campaign activity
Prediction markets price the race at roughly 99 percent Democratic
No public polling or expert ratings flag the race as competitive
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: a D+13 district, an incumbent with a massive money advantage, a challenger with no reported fundraising, and markets pricing Huffman near 99 percent. With no contrary evidence, the fundamentals-based margin of roughly 22 points stands with modestly tightened uncertainty.
model.watch: Any reported fundraising by Littau, outside spending in the district, or a surprise poll showing a single-digit race would be the first sign the contest is closer than it appears.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's second district covers the North Coast, including Marin, Sonoma, and neighboring counties, territory that has favored Democrats by double digits in recent cycles. Jared Huffman has held the seat since 2013 and returns with more than $1.1 million in cash on hand. His Republican challenger, Robin Littau, shows no reported fundraising in available records, and no outside groups are spending in the race.

No public polls cover the contest, and no national raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets put Huffman's chances near 99 percent. The combination of a favorable district, a well-funded incumbent, and a challenger with little visible campaign activity points to a comfortable Democratic hold, with the main uncertainty being turnout in a low-profile general election rather than the outcome itself.
